rationale: A wins because it gives the founder five usable story shapes and tells them exactly where each one collapses if the missing facts stay missing. Its strongest line, "Wise will roll out stablecoin settlement one regulator at a time," finds the real policy story in the rollout constraint; B gets close with "Wise's stablecoin rolls out market by market," but then calls it "defensive-comment," which is the wrong story type and a small tell that the strategy is less controlled. B also lets slop creep into the trend headline with "the trend a market's edge case becomes its plumbing"; A states the category story cleanly without pretending one launch proves the market.
gaps_in_A: "A listed, profitable payments company is now settling business transfers in stablecoin" is a little close to a company-exists/category note unless Wise can supply the named instrument, partner, and expected volume share.

"Investors will ask what stablecoin settlement does to Wise's margins" is smart, but it may be too thin for markets press without any disclosed economics; A flags that, but the angle still depends on a CFO giving numbers.

"Wise will roll out stablecoin settlement one regulator at a time" says the first-market decision is news, but the update does not name the first market. A catches this in proof, yet the headline currently outruns the supplied facts by half a step.
gaps_in_B: "A profitable, public fintech moving £30B a quarter just embraced stablecoins — the trend a market's edge case becomes its plumbing" is overwrought and grammatically bent. More important, it flirts with proving a trend from one company while warning not to do exactly that.

"Wise routes cross-border business payments through a regulated stablecoin, skipping correspondent banks" overstates the mechanics. The update says faster and cheaper than correspondent banking, not that Wise is fully skipping correspondent banks or which leg is replaced.
"Story type: defensive-comment" on the regulatory rollout angle is wrong. This is a policy/regulatory trend angle, not a defensive comment; labels matter when a founder is choosing what to pitch.

B only gives three angles and misses useful second-wave shapes A catches, especially the investor-margin question and the named-customer treasury story. Those are not padding; they are different desks with different proof needs.
